assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Neutron
items.clue: An uncharged particle found in the nucleus alongside the protons.

items.label: Nuclear model
items.clue: Nearly all the mass and all the positive charge sit in a tiny centre, with the electrons outside it.

items.label: Alpha particle scattering experiment
items.clue: Its results showed that the mass of an atom is concentrated at its centre.

items.label: Energy level
items.clue: One of the different distances from the nucleus at which electrons in an atom are arranged.

questions.stem: What should happen to an accepted scientific model when new experimental evidence does not fit it?

options.text: The model is kept, since it is proved
The evidence is put down to an error
The model is changed or is replaced
The model is kept and the result ignored

questions.explanation: New experimental evidence may lead to a scientific model being changed or replaced.

questions.stem: How were atoms described before the discovery of the electron?

options.text: As tiny spheres that could not be divided at all
As tiny spheres with a nucleus at their centre
As balls of positive charge full of electrons
As clouds of charge with no definite shape

questions.explanation: Before the discovery of the electron, atoms were thought to be tiny spheres that could not be divided.

questions.stem: What did the plum pudding model suggest about the atom?

options.text: The atom has a small positive nucleus with electrons orbiting
The atom is a ball of positive charge with electrons in it
The atom is a ball of negative charge with protons in it
The atom is a solid sphere that cannot be split at all

questions.explanation: The plum pudding model suggested that the atom is a ball of positive charge with negative electrons embedded in it.

questions.stem: In the alpha particle scattering experiment, what happened to most of the alpha particles?

options.text: They bounced straight back from the metal foil
They were deflected by exactly the same angle
They passed straight through the metal foil
They were absorbed and stopped in the foil

questions.explanation: Most alpha particles passed straight through, which showed that the atom is mostly empty space.

questions.stem: What is the key difference between the plum pudding model and the nuclear model?

options.text: The nuclear model has the electrons embedded in charge
The plum pudding model has a nucleus at its centre
The plum pudding model gave the atom a net charge
The nuclear model puts the charge at the centre

questions.explanation: In the nuclear model the mass of an atom is concentrated at the centre and that nucleus is charged, rather than the charge being spread through the whole atom.

questions.stem: What did Niels Bohr add to the nuclear model of the atom?

options.text: Electrons may orbit the nucleus at any distance
Electrons orbit the nucleus at specific distances only
The nucleus lies at the centre and holds the mass
The nucleus contains neutrons as well as protons

questions.explanation: Bohr adapted the nuclear model by suggesting that electrons orbit the nucleus at specific distances, and his calculations agreed with observations.

questions.stem: Later experiments showed that the positive charge of any nucleus could be subdivided. What followed from this?

options.text: The nuclear charge was shown to be a single indivisible lump
The neutron was named, a particle carrying no charge
The proton was named, each carrying equal positive charge
The nucleus itself was shown to be negatively charged

questions.explanation: The charge was found to be a whole number of equal smaller particles, and the name proton was given to these particles.

questions.stem: What did the experimental work of James Chadwick provide evidence for?

options.text: The existence of a nucleus in every atom
The existence of protons inside all atomic nuclei
The existence of electron energy levels in atoms
The existence of neutrons within the nucleus

questions.explanation: Chadwick's experimental work provided the evidence to show the existence of neutrons within the nucleus.

questions.stem: Why did the scattering experiment lead scientists to change the model of the atom?

options.text: A few alpha particles bounced back, which the old model forbade
Scientists preferred the newer picture because it was simpler to draw
Every alpha particle bounced back, showing the atom is solid all through
Nearly all the alpha particles bounced straight back off the foil

questions.explanation: A ball of evenly spread positive charge could not repel a fast alpha particle backwards, so the evidence forced a new model with a tiny, dense, charged nucleus.
